ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A circular conducting coil a lies flat on a horizontal tabletop, and a vertical solenoid b is fixed directly above a, with their axes coinciding. Solenoid b, a power supply, and a sliding rheostat are connected into the circuit as shown in the figure. If the slider P of the sliding rheostat is slid downward, how will the pressure FN of coil a on the horizontal tabletop change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The pressure FN of coil a on the horizontal table will increase
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the circular ring-shaped conducting coil a lies flat on a horizontal tabletop; the vertical solenoid b is fixed directly above a, and the axes of the two coincide. Solenoid b forms a closed circuit with the power supply on the right and the sliding rheostat, the sliding contact is labeled P, and the figure shows the sliding rheostat connected in series in the solenoid circuit. Then reason: According to the connection method of the sliding rheostat in the figure, when sliding contact P slides downward, the effective resistance connected into the circuit decreases, so the current in solenoid b increases. The increase in current makes the magnetic field produced by solenoid b at the lower coil a strengthen, and the magnetic flux through coil a increases. According to Lenz's law, the induced current produced in coil a must hinder this increase in magnetic flux, so coil a and solenoid b manifest as mutually repelling each other. Since b is above a, the direction of the repulsive force acting on a is downward. Thus the pressure of coil a on the tabletop equals its gravity plus the downward magnetic force, so the pressure FN increases.
